name: tree
title: Tree (hierarchy)
tagline: Top-down hierarchy tree — a root and its branching children as labelled boxes joined by connectors; tidy auto-layout, optional Yes/No edge labels, every box occludable.
description: A top-down hierarchical tree: a root box at the top, its children below, their children below them — the picture for any multi-level hierarchy (taxonomy and classification, decision trees, family trees, syntax-parse trees, concept hierarchies). You author only the hierarchy — a flat list of boxes, each naming its parent, with exactly one root — and the model derives every box position from a tidy-tree layout (a parent centres over its children; disjoint branches never overlap), sizes each box to its wrapped label, and draws and trims every connector. Connectors can carry an edge label ("Yes"/"No") for a decision tree. Any box occludes to "?" for "name this group", boxes highlight in amber to mark an answer or trace a path, and `reveal` shows the tree one level at a time for a grow-it staged build. For a process with loops and merging arrows use diagram/flowchart; for a single hub with one ring of branches use diagram/mind-map.
whenToUse: Reach for this for a hierarchy drawn top-down: a root that splits into children, which split again — a taxonomy or classification (kingdom → phylum → class; quadrilaterals → rhombus / kite), a decision / sorting tree (use edgeLabel "Yes"/"No" on each branch), a family or dynasty tree, a syntax-parse tree, or a concept hierarchy. Author the nodes as a flat list: give each a unique id and a label, and set parentId to the box it hangs under — leave parentId off the one root. The layout, box sizes and connectors are all derived, so you never position anything. Conventions: exactly one node omits parentId; on a decision tree put the branch wording in each child's edgeLabel. Questions: set a box's occlude to ask "name this group / what belongs here?" (the rest of the tree stays visible); highlight a box to mark the answer or to light up a classification path. Staged builds: set reveal to grow the tree one level per stage (root first), or move a highlight down a path stage by stage — the tree never reflows. Keep the same tree across the blocks of one lesson. Synonyms a teacher might use: tree diagram, hierarchy, taxonomy, classification, classify, sorting tree, decision tree, family tree, branching diagram, parse tree, concept hierarchy. Switch model when the picture changes: a step-by-step process with yes/no decisions, loops or arrows that merge is diagram/flowchart; a single central idea with one ring of related branches (no deeper nesting) is diagram/mind-map; a word split into prefix·root·suffix is diagram/etymology.

id.description: Unique kebab-case id for this box, referenced by other nodes' parentId (e.g. "animals", "vertebrates"). Not shown to pupils — the wiring handle.

parentId.description: Id of this node's parent box. Omit on EXACTLY ONE node — that node is the root. Every other parentId must name a node in this list (no cycles).

label.description: The text inside the box, wrapped to fit.

image.description: An optional photo shown above the label inside the box (the diagram/cycle image-node pattern) — e.g. a specimen on a classification tree. The model reserves a fixed slot and crops the photo to fill it; the box grows to fit. Photos display on the live web/slide; a static PNG/print/PPTX export shows a labelled placeholder frame until asset-rasterisation lands.

url.description: Absolute image URL — e.g. a Wikimedia Commons upload.wikimedia.org thumbnail. Must be a real, reachable image.

alt.description: A short description of the photo, for accessibility and the figure aria.

aspect.description: Shape of the image slot the photo is cropped to fill. Default "landscape" (4:3). Keep one aspect across the tree so the boxes match.

edgeLabel.description: Optional label drawn on the connector from this node UP to its parent — the branch outcome on a decision tree, e.g. "Yes" / "No". Omit on a plain hierarchy edge.

occlude.description: Render this box's label as "?" — the question hook ("name this group / what goes here?"). The box and connectors stay drawn and the hidden word never leaks into the aria. Default false.

occludeImage.description: Blank this box's photo to a "?" placeholder (the photo would otherwise give the answer away). Ignored when there is no image. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this box — the answer, or a box on a traced classification path. Default false.

color.description: Override THIS box's colour (an explicit author/teacher request — "make this box dark green"). Every box is a single neutral grey by default, so set this to COLOUR-CODE a subtree — e.g. give each top-level branch and its descendants a different colour. Wins over the figure-wide `colors.nodes`. A reserved role keyword (accent, accent-2…accent-5, ink, muted, scaffold) keeps it brand-themeable; a colour literal (#hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), or a CSS named colour like "teal" or "darkgreen") is honoured exactly and opts this box OUT of brand reskinning. Ignored on a highlighted box (amber is reserved for the answer). Omit for the neutral default.

nodes.description: The boxes of the tree as a flat list. Exactly one node omits parentId (the root); every other node names its parent. Order does not matter — positions are derived.

reveal.description: Draw only the top N levels (the root is level 1). Omit to show the whole tree. Use across staged steps (1, 2, 3, …) to grow the tree one level at a time — boxes never move as levels appear.

orientation.description: Growth direction: "down" (default) puts the root at the top and grows downward; "right" puts the root on the left and grows rightward (handy for a deep, narrow tree). Keep it consistent across a lesson.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

colors.description: Optional figure-wide colour overrides — set ONLY when an author/teacher explicitly asks ("make the boxes dark green", "the connectors should be grey"). Omit to keep the themeable defaults (accent-blue boxes, neutral-grey connectors), which follow a brand reskin. A per-node `color` overrides this for one box.

nodes.description: Colour of every (non-highlighted) box, replacing the default accent blue. A reserved role keyword (accent, accent-2…accent-5, ink, muted, scaffold) stays brand-themeable; a colour literal (#hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), or a CSS named colour like "teal") is honoured exactly and opts the boxes OUT of brand reskinning. A single box can still differ via its own `color`.

connectors.description: Colour of every parent→child connector line. Same value space as `nodes`. Connectors are one shared group per parent, so this is figure-wide — there is no per-edge connector colour.

examples.label: Worked taxonomy — classifying living things (three levels)
Decision tree — sorting a quadrilateral (edge labels Yes/No)
Occluded question — name the hidden group
Blank answer space — complete the bottom row
Hard case — deep, unbalanced taxonomy with a wide level
Author-set colours — colour-code the branches + figure-wide connectors
